title: Writing God Bless the Child for Joe Romano with Buddy Rich
summary: He wrote the chart in a day for Joe Romano at a Boston club, leaving the second chorus open for the soloist.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, you know I wrote a chart for Buddy, we were in Boston at Lenny’s on the Turnpike. It was “God Bless the Child.” And I wrote it for Joe Romano, a great alto

player. You probably knew Joe, I’m sure. And so I wrote it in a day, because he wanted it the next night. And I brought it in and I really was pleased with it. And you know, in the second chorus there was nothing except the rhythm section and Joe, all that nice space. Because most soloists don’t like backgrounds underneath them. They want that freedom to take it wherever they want to go. And then that night after the gig Buddy says, “Fill that in, I don’t like that, it’s too much open space, fill that in.” And he made me put backgrounds in and that’s the public arrangement that’s out there now. But he wanted that filled in. He liked that have that fullness. I like to hear the space for the soloist. And when they’re done then I’ll bring the band back in.
